title: Input-read presence is preserved
statement: Let $W$ be a finite-state binary machine, $a$ a natural number, $x$ a Boolean input word, and $c$ a configuration of $W$ on $x$. Replacing each nonblank symbol read by the clock-stage configuration with false, while leaving a blank read blank, gives the same possibly blank symbol as applying that replacement to the symbol read by $c$.
hypotheses_covered: configuration c of W on x
replaced:
Let $W$ be a binary machine, $a$ a padding constant, and $c$ a configuration of $W$ on
an input $x$.  After forgetting the bit values (retaining only whether a symbol is
present), the symbol read by the input head of the clock-stage configuration of $c$
agrees with the correspondingly masked native read of $c$.
